AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: To understand the role of magnetization transfer ratio in identifying patients with clinically significant myelopathy and disability.

AbstractText.Label: SUMMARY OF BACKGROUND DATA
AbstractText.content: Magnetization transfer ratio (MTR) is a quantitative measure that correlates with myelin loss and neural tissue destruction in a variety of neurological diseases. However, the usefulness of MTR in patients with cervical spondylotic myelopathy (CSM) has not been examined.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: We prospectively enrolled seven CSM patients and seven age-matched controls to undergo MRI imaging of the cervical spine. Nurick, Neck Disability Index (NDI), and modified Japanese Orthopedic Association (mJOA) scores were collected for all patients. Clinical hyperreflexia was tested at the MCP joint, using a 6-axis load cell. Reflex was simulated by quickly moving the joint from maximum flexion to maximum extension (300 °/sec). Anterior, lateral, and posterior cord MTR measurements were compared to clinical outcomes.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Compared to controls, CSM patients had lower anterior cord MTR (38.29 v. 29.97, Δ = -8.314, p = 0.0022), and equivalent posterior cord (p = 0.2896) and lateral cord (p = 0.3062) MTR. Higher Nurick scores were associated with lower anterior cord MTR (p = 0.0205), but not lateral cord (p = 0.5446) or posterior cord MTR (p = 0.1222). Lower mJOA was associated with lower anterior cord MTR (p = 0.0090), but not lateral cord (p = 0.4864) or posterior cord MTR (p = 0.4819). There was no association between NDI and MTR of the anterior (p = 0.4351), lateral (p = 0.7557), or posterior cord (p = 0.9171). There was a linear relationship between hyperreflexia and anterior cord MTR (slope = -117.3, R = 0.6598, p = 0.0379), but not lateral cord (p = 0.1906, R = 0.4511) or posterior cord (p = 0.2577, R = 0.3957) MTR.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: Anterior cord MTR correlates with clinical outcomes as measured by mJOA index, Nurick score, and quantitative hyperreflexia, and could play a role in the preoperative assessment of CSM.

Article.ArticleTitle: Quantitative Magnetization Transfer MRI Measurements of the Anterior Spinal cord Region are Associated with Clinical Outcomes in Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy.
